newsitem.title: USA: Navy plane crashes at Air Force base in Alabama.
newsitem.headline: Navy plane crashes at Air Force base in Alabama.

text.p: A Navy instructor pilot and student were killed Monday when their training plane crashed while they were trying to land at Maxwell Air Force Base in Alabama, the base said.

The crew members were rushed to a base hospital by members of an emergency rescue unit but were later pronounced dead. The Air Force did not identify them pending notification of relatives but said they were an instructor pilot and student.
It also said in a statement that officials reported no fire was involved in the crash. CNN quoted sources as saying the plane appeared to have engine trouble before the crash.

Air Force Lt. John Redfield said the plane, a Navy T-34 trainer, crashed at about 10 a.m. EST (1400 GMT) after leaving Pensacola Naval Air Station, about 160 miles (250 km) away on the Florida panhandle.
"It crashed as it was approaching the runway," he said.
Redfield could not say whether the Air Force base was the plane's intended destination. No further details of the crash were available.
Redfield said a board of military officers would be convened to investigate the crash, the fourth involving a military plane within the past two weeks.
An HC-130 cargo plane with 11 crew members went down in the Pacific Ocean off the California coast on Nov. 22. One crew member survived.

An Air Force F-16 fighter plane crashed near Tulsa, Oklahoma, on Nov. 21, but the pilot ejected safely. An Air National Guard F-16D fighter plane crashed in an Ohio forest during a training mission Nov. 27. Both pilots ejected safely.
